output.root_cause: The `refund_status` tool contract is mislabelled: its description says "Check **and process** the refund status for an order" while it is in fact an idempotent read that returns a byte-identical payload on every call. Combined with the system prompt's imperative "Don't leave a refund request half-finished — if there is more you can do to get the customer paid, go ahead and do it rather than just describing the situation back to them", the agent believes re-invoking `refund_status` is a way to push the refund forward. Nothing in the prompt or tool set defines the correct terminal behaviour for `state=processing` (send `refund_delay_notice`, escalate when `sla_breached=true`, or simply report the state), so re-polling becomes the default 'action'.
output.mechanism: 1) User asks for refund status; agent runs `order_lookup` (status=delivered) then `refund_status`, which returns `state=processing`, `completed_at=null`, `processor_ref=null` (tr_000559, tr_000157, tr_000170, tr_000597). 2) This payload gives the agent no completion it can report and no next-step affordance: `refund_execute` would be a duplicate payment against an already-open refund, so the model avoids it. 3) The prompt forbids merely 'describing the situation back' to the customer, and the tool description promises that `refund_status` also 'processes', so on each follow-up turn ("can you check again?", "any update since we last looked?") the agent re-issues the identical `refund_status` call. 4) Because the tool is a pure read, the result is bit-for-bit identical, producing the cluster signature n_refund_status=2.91 and max_repeat_identical_call=2.91 vs cohort 1.30, and the elevated cost signal (0.77 vs same-intent peers) with no compensating state change. 5) The available legitimate exits are never taken: n_send_email=0.00 (cohort 0.98) — no `refund_delay_notice` even when `sla_breached=true` (tr_000559 at 116.7h, tr_000170 at 52.9h) — and no `escalate_to_human` despite the prompt's instruction to escalate customers who seem 'like they've been waiting too long'. 6) Under the closing pressure of 'Your goal at the end of every conversation is for the customer to feel confident that their money is on its way', the agent then emits a final message unsupported by the tool payload: 'Your refund shows as completed on our end already' while `state=processing`/`completed_at=null` (tr_000170, tr_000597), and 'I don't see a refund on file for this order yet' although `refund_id=rfd_000102` was returned (tr_000157). Only tr_000559 closes with a statement consistent with the data.
output.why_it_recurs: It is a deterministic interaction between a static tool description and a static prompt directive, not a stochastic slip. Every refund_status_inquiry where the refund is legitimately mid-flight (`state=processing`) lands the agent in the same dead end: the 'and process' wording promises progress the tool cannot deliver, the read is idempotent so retrying never changes the input, the prompt bans a purely informational answer, and there is no stated policy mapping `state=processing` / `sla_breached` to `send_email` or `escalate_to_human`. Any follow-up user turn re-triggers the same loop, which is why the cluster is tight (23 traces, ~3 identical calls each) and why it was found by shape/cost anomaly detection rather than by a rule.
output.remediation_summary: Fix the tool contract wording and add an explicit terminal policy. (1) Rename the `refund_status` description to 'Read-only: returns the current refund record for an order. It does not create, advance, or process a refund; repeated calls in the same conversation return identical data and have no effect.' (2) Add to the system prompt: if `state=processing`, do not call `refund_status` again for that order — report the state from the data you already have. (3) Define the allowed next actions explicitly: when `state=processing` and `sla_breached=true` (or the customer follows up again), call `escalate_to_human` with the SLA breach as the reason and/or `send_email` with template `refund_delay_notice`; only call `refund_execute` when no refund record exists. (4) Constrain the closing message: never tell a customer a refund is completed unless `completed_at` is non-null, and never say no refund exists when a `refund_id` was returned; soften the 'don't just describe the situation' / 'money is on its way' instructions so that an accurate status report is an acceptable ending. Optionally, as defence in depth (code), have the orchestrator dedupe or reject identical read calls with the same arguments within a conversation.
